translationRepairs: I would punish poseurs who feign sainthood and bring down slanderers like Zang Cang;
I would punish Li Chu for obstructing the sage and chastise Zang Cang for slandering the wise;

誅犁鋤之介聖兮，討臧倉之訴知 names Li Chu parallel to Zang Cang, so erasing 犁鋤 as generic "poseurs" is wrong; but 介聖 means interposing against / obstructing the sage, not posing as one, and 訴知 is Zang Cang's slander of the wise.

Then I would shut my gate to study moral teaching and read Confucius and Laozi, hoping for something of the immortals' ease; I would climb the Long ridges and high hills, send my spirit wandering through heaven and earth, and let my eyes sweep the eight reaches of the world.

Then I would shut my gate to study moral teaching and read Confucius and Laozi, hoping for something of the blessing of Chisongzi and Wangzi Qiao; I would climb the Long ridges and high hills, send my spirit wandering through heaven and earth, and let my eyes sweep the eight reaches of the world.

庶幾乎松、喬之福 names the immortals Song/Chisongzi and Qiao/Wangzi Qiao and seeks their 福 (blessing), so "immortals' ease" erases the names and mistranslates 福; the proposal's bracketed "[Chisongzi] Song" is still awkward for idiomatic English.
